H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper distinguishes auto mode and manual mode, but does not define nested/composite states with internal substates.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Control decisions depend on sensor thresholds: pH 6-9, TDS/conductivity <1500 ppm for discharge, and >1500 ppm for return to equalization.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: PLC actions drive many outputs: pumps, mixers, solenoid valves, motorized valve openings, alarms, indicators, and HMI monitoring/read-write commands.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper mentions abnormal plant conditions and corrective actions by the user, but gives no explicit recovery transition or safe-state path.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Mode names appear in the flow-chart section, I/O actions in the PLC block, HMI actions in interface design, and quality guards in the water-quality discussion.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as manual mode, closed-loop system, bypass, and abnormal circumstances imply operator override and feedback-control behavior beyond a flat event list.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are narrated across prose sections rather than attached to formal state definitions, e.g. manual mode actions and bypass actions are described separately.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The paper gives threshold guards, but no explicit transition guard combining multiple variables with arithmetic or boolean composition.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No parent/composite state with its own entry, during, or exit behavior is specified.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No from-any-state fault or emergency transition is declared.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain is present.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: Quality logic can be modeled with threshold expressions such as pH in 6-9 and TDS/conductivity below or above 1500 ppm.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Continuous HMI monitoring of plant status, analog values, and active actuators is a cross-cutting during-style behavior across the controller.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Some actions are abstract monitoring/alerting side effects, but many outputs are concrete relays, valves, pumps, and interface commands.

key_nl_quotes: If the reading value is in the safe number, the water will be discharged into the water channel.
If water is > 1500 ppm, it will flow back to the equalization unit.
one_line_pitch: This is a strong action-and-guard stress test where auto/manual supervisory control, feedback routing, and HMI monitoring are scattered across the paper rather than stated as one clean FSM.
rationale: The sample has limited hierarchy and only vague fault handling, but it is strong on the baseline-weak dimensions of actions and guarded control. The PLC supervises many concrete actuators and monitoring outputs while making feedback decisions from pH and conductivity/TDS thresholds. Its key state, guard, and action information is distributed across flow-chart, I/O, interface, and water-quality sections, making it a realistic stress test for semantic attribution.
